entries.title: SDK update: model-provider

ai.title: SDK final refusals now include free mode rate limits
ai.summary: The SDK model provider in sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts now treats a 429 response with the error code free_mode_rate_limited as a final, non-retryable refusal when the Retry-After header is 60 seconds or more. This prevents the AI SDK from ignoring the long wait and retrying on its own 2-8 second backoff, which previously caused a Desktop or Cloud model start to refund the purchase and surface a misleading session superseded 409 error instead of the rate limit message. The change adds a conditional when predicate to the final refusal matcher that checks the server's Retry-After value against AI_SDK_MAX_HONOURED_RETRY_AFTER_MS; shorter waits are still retried by the AI SDK as before. A new test file verifies that a daily-window refusal is refused once, keeps the server's copy, and never reaches the refunded-start 409.
ai.evidence: sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts adds a fourth entry to FINAL_REFUSALS for 'free_mode_rate_limited' (429) with a when predicate that returns true only when retryAfterMsOf(response) >= AI_SDK_MAX_HONOURED_RETRY_AFTER_MS (60_000); the new test file sdk/src/impl/__tests__/free-mode-rate-limit-no-retry.test.ts asserts that a daily-window refusal is refused once and never reaches the refunded-start 409.

eli5.text: The assistant now recognizes long waits for free models as final limits instead of temporary errors. It applies when a free request is denied and the server says to wait a minute or longer; shorter waits are still retried as before. You will immediately see that you have hit a free-model limit and can try later, rather than being told your purchase was refunded and your session ended.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: device-execution

ai.title: Add elevation deadline constants and operation timeout helper
ai.summary: The shared desktop-cloud module now defines `DEVICE_ELEVATION_APPROVAL_MS` at 10 minutes and `DEVICE_ELEVATION_COMMAND_MS` at 5 minutes, combined with a 1-minute buffer into the new `DEVICE_ELEVATION_MS` deadline. These values prevent the Cloud server from refusing Desktop's answers with a 504 error when a user takes a few minutes to approve an elevated command or the command runs for a while. A new `deviceOperationMs` helper function returns this extended deadline specifically for `request_elevation` tool requests, while all other mutating operations retain the standard `DEVICE_EXEC_MS` cap. The change addresses a scenario where the default execution window was too short for elevation workflows, causing Cloud to time out before the Desktop could apply its changes.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `DEVICE_ELEVATION_APPROVAL_MS`, `DEVICE_ELEVATION_COMMAND_MS`, and `DEVICE_ELEVATION_MS` constants, and the `deviceOperationMs` function to `common/src/desktop-cloud/device-execution.ts`.

eli5.text: The system now allows up to 21 minutes for permission approvals and commands that require extra clearance, instead of the previous five-minute limit. This applies to users running the desktop app when they ask the assistant to perform actions that need their explicit sign-off. Previously, if you took a few minutes to approve a request or the command ran longer than expected, the cloud service would stop waiting and report an error. Now, the service will wait longer so your approval and the command can finish successfully.
